author: Sofia Alvarez
title: European Leaders Visit Moldova Amid Russian Interference Fears
text:
• Leaders from France, Germany, and Poland visited Moldova on August 28, 2024.
• The visit coincided with Moldova's 34th independence anniversary from the Soviet Union.
• French President Emmanuel Macron, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk attended the meeting in Chisinau.
• Moldovan President Maia Sandu warned of significant Russian interference in the upcoming parliamentary elections scheduled for September 28.
• The European leaders expressed support for Moldova's pro-Western path and EU aspirations.
• Macron stated the visit aimed to demonstrate that 'Moldova matters and that its future lies with Europe and the European Union.'
• Sandu emphasized that Russian interference poses a 'direct threat to our national security, sovereignty, and our country’s European future.'
• Russia has denied allegations of meddling in Moldova's affairs.
• Moldova was granted EU candidate status in 2022, and accession negotiations began last year.
• Moldovan voters narrowly supported the country's EU trajectory in a vote last year.
• Sandu's presidency was secured in a second term during the same year, amid accusations of Russian interference.
• Moldovan officials accuse Russia of waging a 'hybrid war' against the nation, including disinformation and vote-buying.
• Macron pledged France's continued support for Moldova's EU accession process.
• Chancellor Merz warned of daily Russian efforts to disrupt freedom and democracy in Moldova.
• Moldova's ruling Party of Action and Solidarity (PAS) has governed since 2021 but may lose its parliamentary majority in the upcoming elections.
• Cristian Cantir, an associate professor, noted the visit is a show of support for Moldova's pro-European path.
